git.clean_note: `clean` covers the whole worktree; `runtime_clean` covers only the files the runtime digest is taken over. A result written into the worktree necessarily observes clean=false.

lineage.runtime_last_changed_subject: fix: fit the Provenance role column to its real labels (RB-2)
commits_since_on_head: b37c1fe bind the RB2-A1 acceptance set to one runtime head
c483bda add the RB2-A1 manifest verifier
e7a9a1a docs: deny RB-2 review 1 for unbound acceptance evidence
4247e7c docs: RB-2 is IMPLEMENTED — AWAITING ADVERSARIAL REVIEW
lineage.note: if runtime_files_changed_since is empty, every commit between runtime_last_changed_at and the acceptance head is non-runtime (documentation/records), so the generated corpus carries the final production behaviour even though the head is later

runtime.note: runtime digests are taken over LINE-ENDING-NORMALISED content of every tracked runtime file, so they are reproducible from any checkout of the same commit and are unaffected by later documentation-only commits

frozen_sources.note: the inputs both code trees read. The base checkout reaches these same directories through junctions, so base and head did not merely read equal bytes — they read the same files.

deliverables.note: every file of every produced corpus: workbooks, their outcome/provenance sidecars, peer payload envelopes, ownership markers and evidence artifacts

harness.note: the acceptance scripts that produced every result here. Not product runtime, so deliberately outside the runtime digest; bound by content so the exact code is identifiable and can be supplied and checked against these digests.

committed_oracle.note: imported by the harness, not reimplemented, so the product check and the acceptance oracle cannot diverge

committed_verifier.note: independent re-implementation used to check this manifest; deliberately does NOT share code with it

results.note: every retained result, bound by content. Judged over the CLAIMED (acceptance) class: those must carry the head runtime digest. Base-side results carry the base runtime; history is retained and claims nothing.

base_side.reason: the base corpus's own build record, written by the BASE checkout before runtime stamping existed. The base corpus is bound instead by content (its root digest below) and by base-identity.json, which proves the base tree is byte-identical in content to 896083e014d0451d5b05e5b6b024339aebc84d74
proves the base checkout == the recorded base commit; carries the BASE runtime stamp, the same digest invariance.json records as runtime_base

source_records.reason: the normalised TSN library's own rebuild record — it describes how a frozen INPUT was built, not a result of the head runtime. It cannot be re-run under the head without rebuilding the library, which would destroy the very frozen-input identity this acceptance set depends on. It is vouched for instead by frozen-inputs.json, which IS head-stamped and proves all 8 datasets still hash to exactly what this recorded
